dedupe_keys.name: gym anm active network management environments

description: Gym-ANM provides Python reinforcement-learning environments for active management of electricity distribution networks. Robin Henry maintains the package, developed with Damien Ernst. It exposes configurable grid tasks through Gymnasium, with a documented ANM6Easy example and scripts for agent-environment interaction. Inputs define the task and control actions; outputs are observations, rewards and optional rendered states. Coverage is global and network-specific, with task time steps determined by configuration, not a fixed observation dataset. Public code, pip installation and documentation are free under MIT. A limitation is that environment construction determines physical and operational realism; a successful benchmark does not establish safe operation on a real grid. The current README requires Python 3.10 or later and warns that some Windows rendering features are untested. Gym-ANM supports comparison of control policies and can complement power-flow studies in pandapower (model-pandapower). Two 2021 articles describe the environments and software. No learning agent or power-network scenario was executed.
